title: Research question and lending decision
summary: Estimate charge-off probability before money is committed. Keep prediction, policy and calculation separate.

title: How the evidence changed our decisions
summary: The results changed the questions about model complexity, calibration, pricing and serving.

title: Data source, population and sampling
summary: The sample covers accepted loans with resolved outcomes, sampled from every chunk.

title: Which fields can the model use?
summary: Separate information available before pricing from incumbent decisions, targets and later outcomes.

title: The 64-column working dataset
summary: Six loaded groups have different modelling and business roles.

title: What the lender could know before pricing
summary: Eligibility depends on the decision point, even when later information would improve the score.

title: What counts as a bad loan?
summary: The charge-off label defines the population and outcome that the probability can describe.

title: Cleaning before modelling
summary: Keep deterministic parsing separate from training-fitted transformations.

title: What the data changed
summary: Drift, missingness and borrower patterns motivated choices while exposing weaknesses in the experiment.

title: Feature engineering
summary: Three domain hypotheses become inputs; the stated admission rule is not enforced.

title: The final 56 conceptual model inputs
summary: Conceptual inputs and transformed columns are different counts.

title: How features were selected
summary: The final list is explicit; the original field screening still needs a defensible record.

title: Testing on later loans
summary: Chronological evaluation reveals transfer problems that a mixed random split can conceal.

title: Preparing inputs for the models
summary: Imputation and encoding make inputs usable without establishing that their information is valid.

title: What each model comparison tests
summary: Separate the value of information, model complexity and probability calibration.

title: Why logistic regression
summary: A simple probability model supplies a credible reference for extra complexity.

title: Why XGBoost
summary: Nonlinear interactions may help, but later-cohort evidence must justify complexity.

title: Hyperparameter selection
summary: Temporal cross-validation selects parameters within training.

title: Evaluation metrics from first principles
summary: Separate ranking, probability error and threshold behaviour from pricing utility.

title: Controlled comparisons and uncertainty
summary: Five paired questions test model strength and incremental information.

title: Calibration
summary: Pricing consumes probabilities, so ranking alone is not enough.

title: Operating point and threshold policy
summary: A score does not approve a loan. Cutoffs need a separate decision rule.

title: Feature importance and error analysis
summary: Predictive reliance is not causality, fairness or a local explanation.

title: From PD to LGD to price
summary: Loss severity is measured; funding and margin are assumed; price is calculated.

title: Pricing back-test
summary: Compare predicted loss with realised principal loss; do not confuse a simulation with a valid offer.

title: Training versus serving reality
summary: Full-feature research metrics do not validate the reduced browser form.

title: How an application becomes a result
summary: Trace where the system predicts, calculates, defaults information and applies policy.

title: Reproducibility and artifacts
summary: Reading recorded evidence, evaluating a frozen artifact and retraining are different activities.

title: Getting the model into a running service
summary: A reproducible prediction, an active release and a valid lending model require different evidence.

title: What the corrections did not solve
summary: Each correction changed one failure mode; it did not validate the next stage automatically.

title: Fairness, governance and responsible use
summary: No completed fairness study or approved underwriting policy is evidenced.

title: When the results stop being reliable
summary: Check the conditions behind a claim before transferring it to new applicants or decisions.

title: Which experiments matter next?
summary: Resolve population and serving gaps before spending effort on further model complexity.

title: Checking the evidence
summary: Find the record that answers your question and judge whether it supports the conclusion.
